readerQuestion: How can my household share a Home Assistant shopping list across phones, and what happens when the shopper has no internet connection?
directAnswer: Use the built-in Shopping list and select the same todo entity on both household phones. Verify a shared edit and completion at home, then test mobile-data access. Remote access still requires connectivity; use a complete screenshot as a read-only fallback or verify a separate phone app workflow. Optional iOS Reminders sync is experimental and depends on phone permissions and scheduled execution.
originalContribution: Section 3 supplies an original Alex/Sam grocery-trip rehearsal with two items, a quantity edit, a completion and a mobile-data addition, each paired with an expected result. Section 4 separates local server storage, remote connectivity and offline copies, with a harmless disconnected-use check. The final decision table maps five disagreements to specific first checks. These are illustrative procedures, not reported deployment measurements.
limitations: No Home Assistant installation, iOS device, OurGroceries app or grocery trip was tested. The browser checks verify website presentation only. Reminders Sync documentation remains a maintainer draft, so key behavior was cross-checked in released iOS 2026.9.2 source; installed app versions may differ and iOS does not guarantee background scheduling. No unsupported offline-sync claim is made for OurGroceries. Screenshots cannot sync purchases. The illustration is generated and does not depict a real Tara installation.

claimChecks.claim: Shopping list is built in and supports Assist add-item commands; using the list does not itself set up microphones or speech processing.

A To-do list card targets one entity; hide_completed hides the completed section, while its false setting leaves completions visible for verification. The supplied four-line configuration belongs to a dashboard card.
Local to-do creates separate local lists; a todo entity state counts incomplete items rather than containing their text.

The Companion app must reach its Home Assistant address; remote access and no-signal phone use are different prerequisites. The suggested test changes only a phone connection and harmless grocery entries, then restores connectivity.
View visibility hides the tab but not URL access, so a grocery-only dashboard is not a list-only security boundary.
A non-admin account does not by itself define per-list authorization; use separate trusted household logins and do not promise restricted guest access from hidden cards.

Reminders Sync is iOS-only LABS from app 2026.8.0, pairs existing lists, needs full Reminders permission and can propagate deletions in two-way mode. The linked maintainer setup document is still a draft, explicitly disclosed.

Released iOS 2026.9.2 RemindersSyncSettings defaults foreground/background intervals to zero; RemindersSyncBackgroundRefresher treats an interval as an earliest requested execution, with iOS deciding whether to run. No immediate-sync guarantee is made.
OurGroceries connects an account and exposes its own lists through Cloud Polling; installing it is not automatic synchronization of the separate built-in Shopping list.
OurGroceries supports iPhone and Android; its basic app is free with ads and paid ad removal is optional. No price or unverified offline behavior is asserted.
